title: Platform operators — wire shapes, version 1
description: The machine-readable half of platform-operators-v1.contract.yaml. BOTH ARE NORMATIVE TOGETHER. Nothing in this repository executes JSON Schema, so every constraint here is read by a person and hand-implemented: a `required` list is an instruction someone will follow literally (.claude/rules/workflow.md §12).

platformRole.description: The closed union stored in platform_operator.platform_role. An unrecognised stored value denies everything and is never rendered — it collapses to null on read, the device authorization/roles.ts and credential-verifier.ts both use so that a row written by a future migration this build does not understand fails onto the safe path.

operatorSummary.description: NOTE WHAT IS ABSENT AND WHY IT MUST STAY ABSENT: no identifier, no email, no display name, no last-seen. control-plane/0001_principal.sql holds none of them, and it refused an email column outright because 'a directory of every user's personal details, readable without any tenant scope, would be the highest-value target in the system.' AN OPERATOR ROSTER SHOWING EMAIL ADDRESSES WOULD BE THAT DIRECTORY AT THE MOST PRIVILEGED END OF THE PLATFORM. The consequence — an operator cannot tell colleagues apart on screen — is real, is OP-3, and is closed by display names rather than by adding a column here.

created_at.description: RFC 3339, UTC. When platform authority was granted — not when the principal was created.

next_cursor.description: Opaque, bound to the principal and the query shape, exactly as platform-audit-read-v1's. Never constructed or parsed by a client. Null means no further page.

revokeOperatorInput.description:
THE TARGET IS THE PATH PARAMETER, NOT A BODY FIELD — so there is exactly one place it can come from and no possibility of a body and a path disagreeing. THE THREE FIELDS HERE ARE confirmation-v1's confirmedRequestFields, REQUIRED because the permission is `critical` and the requirement derives from sensitivity rather than being declared per route. `reauth_identifier` — RENAMED FROM `identifier` ON 2026-09-05 — is the CALLER'S OWN, and Core must assert the verified credential's principalId equals the calling principal, refusing identically to a wrong password when it does not — without that check, presenting another operator's identifier and password would satisfy re-authentication for your own session. THE CHALLENGE'S `parameters` ARE THIS BODY MINUS THESE THREE FIELDS, UNION THE ROUTE'S DECLARED PATH PARAMETERS — which for this route is the empty object plus `principal_id` — so the binding covers principal_id: a confirmation obtained to revoke operator A cannot be spent revoking operator B.

THE UNION CLAUSE WAS ADDED 2026-09-05 AND WITHOUT IT THIS SENTENCE WAS FALSE. The phrase 'the empty object plus the path parameter' described the result this route needs, but confirmation-v1's rule at the time said body-minus-three and NOTHING ADDED — so the parameters were the empty object, full stop, and the path parameter was in no binding. The sentence asserted the conclusion while citing a rule that contradicted it. confirmation-v1 now defines the union, so the claim holds; see its theSUBMITTEDPARAMETERSAREDEFINED and theBINDINGCOVERSTHEPATHPARAMETERSTOO.

reauth_derived_value.description: 32 bytes, base64url. PBKDF2-SHA256(NFC(password), salt = normalize(reauth_identifier), 600000, 32 bytes) — byte-identical to login, so the client reuses its login code path. NOTE THE SALT IS THE CALLER'S OWN IDENTIFIER, which is what `reauth_` names on both fields. AN AI PRINCIPAL CANNOT PRODUCE THIS, which means no model can ever revoke a platform operator.

reauth_identifier.description:
The CALLER'S OWN login identifier, required because Core cannot recover the KDF salt from a principal — see confirmation-v1 theSALTPROBLEM.

PROPERTY RENAMED 2026-09-05, AND IT LAGGED ITS OWN `required` LIST BY ONE COMMIT. The list was renamed to `reauth_identifier` while this property was left as `identifier`, under `additionalProperties: false` — which made revokeOperatorInput UNSATISFIABLE: every request must carry `reauth_identifier` and no request may carry a field the properties do not declare. Not a stale name; a shape no valid request could match. Found by the Team Lead grepping for bare `identifier` declarations.

CANONICAL DEFINITION: urn:dudo:schema:account-identifier:1#/$defs/accountIdentifier. Restatement, character-identical by obligation.

PATTERN CORRECTED 2026-09-05 from ^[!-?A-~]*@[!-?A-~]*$ (exactly one '@') to at-least-one, matching credential-store.ts. THIS FILE WAS NOT IN THE TWO THE SWEEP WAS ASKED FOR — it was found by grepping for the pattern rather than for the field, and it is the reason that search was the right one: the fourth restatement of a rule is not reliably found by looking where the third was.

principal_id.description: Echoed from the path. It carries nothing the caller did not send.

was_self.description: TRUE WHEN THE OPERATOR REVOKED ITSELF. The console needs it to render the right consequence — a self-revocation means the current session now grants nothing and the operator cannot undo it from the console, which is a materially different screen from having removed a colleague. It is not a security field; it is the difference between 'done' and 'you are locked out, deliberately'.

remaining_operator_count.description: HOW MANY PLATFORM OPERATORS REMAIN. Zero is reachable only by self-revocation of the last operator — revoking ANOTHER principal down to zero is refused with failed_precondition. IT IS RETURNED BECAUSE THE CONSOLE MUST BE ABLE TO SAY 'THERE ARE NOW NO OPERATORS AND RESTORING ONE REQUIRES OUT-OF-BAND ACCESS' at the moment it happens rather than leaving someone to discover it. It discloses nothing: the caller holds core.platform-audit.read and may list the roster directly.
